plain_language_interpretation: The certificate has two different roles: Part I states the sequence leading to death; Part II lists other important conditions that contributed but are not stated as part of that sequence.
BNR_use: Part I is treated as the stated causal sequence; Part II as other significant contributing conditions outside that sequence.
international_rule: Underlying cause is the disease or injury that initiated the train of morbid events; a correctly completed certificate records the starting point on the lowest used Part I line.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: When several Part I lines are used, the lowest used line is an important starting point for underlying-cause selection, but the sequence still has to make sense. BNR therefore treats this as Likely rather than automatically Clear.
BNR_use: A direct target on the lowest used Part I line can reach Likely; multi-line certificates are not promoted to Clear solely because of line position.
international_rule: SP3: when more than one Part I line is used, all entries above must be capable of being caused by the first condition on the lowest used line before that condition is the tentative starting point.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: BNR should not invent causal relationships. A stronger causal rule is added only when an accepted mortality-coding principle or recognised decision table supports it.
BNR_use: Future causal promotions/rejections must cite an explicit WHO rule or recognised mortality decision table rather than clinical intuition.
international_rule: WHO says the special accepted/rejected-sequence instructions must be followed; stated relationships not rejected should be accepted as far as possible; highly improbable relationships should be checked against internationally recognised mortality decision tables.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: ACME is a recognised mortality-coding decision table that can be consulted when WHO Volume 2 does not state a needed causal relationship plainly.
BNR_use: Used as a supplementary provenance source when a required causal pair is not sufficiently explicit in WHO Volume 2.
international_rule: ACME Table D is the causal relationship table used to determine acceptable reported sequences for General Principle/Selection Rules.
source: US National Center for Health Statistics, ICD-10 ACME Decision Tables

plain_language_interpretation: Words such as 'probable', 'possible' or 'presumed' do not make a disease diagnosis disappear for mortality coding. BNR therefore detects the disease wording and handles uncertainty through the certificate/rule context instead.
BNR_use: Words such as probable/possible do not by themselves downgrade an otherwise direct disease expression in the BNR text detector.
international_rule: WHO instructs mortality coders to ignore expressions indicating doubt such as apparently, presumably, probably or possibly.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: If the certificate literally offers Heart and Stroke as alternatives, BNR keeps the combined circulatory evidence but does not force the death into one subtype.
BNR_use: An explicit BNR-Heart-or-Stroke alternative is not forced into either surveillance family. It can support the combined Heart-or-Stroke endpoint while the family remains unresolved.
international_rule: WHO example: 'Stroke or heart attack' is coded to Other and unspecified disorders of circulatory system (I99), because both alternatives are in the circulatory system.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

topic: Target disease above another Part I cause
plain_language_interpretation: Finding Heart or Stroke above another Part I condition proves that the disease was mentioned in the fatal sequence, but it does not by itself prove that it initiated the sequence. BNR therefore normally leaves such cases Possible.
BNR_use: A direct BNR-Heart/BNR-Stroke expression above a lower Part I condition is normally Possible unless a separately documented rule supports stronger attribution.
international_rule: WHO lists acute/subsequent MI and specified cerebrovascular diseases among acute/terminal circulatory diseases that can be accepted as due to malignant neoplasm, diabetes or asthma; therefore disease occurrence above a lower condition does not itself prove that disease is UCoD.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.3A(k) Acute or terminal circulatory diseases due to other conditions

plain_language_interpretation: Some apparently unusual Stroke sequences are explicitly accepted internationally. Any future BNR Stroke causal exception should be tied to a documented rule rather than clinical intuition alone.
BNR_use: Future stroke causal rules must respect explicit accepted sequence exceptions, including specified liver disease and endocarditis relationships.
international_rule: WHO explicitly accepts intracerebral haemorrhage as due to liver disease and specified cerebrovascular embolism/thrombosis/stroke as due to endocarditis.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.3A(h) Cerebrovascular diseases due to other conditions

plain_language_interpretation: A single clean Part I cause gives the strongest certificate structure available to this practical method. If the disease wording is direct and there is no competing ambiguity, BNR allows Clear.
BNR_use: Supports Clear only when one clean Part I line contains direct target wording and no competing target or obvious structural ambiguity.
international_rule: SP2: when only one Part I line is used, the first-mentioned condition is the tentative starting point, followed by checks for further selection/modification rules.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

topic: Ischaemic heart disease with acute myocardial infarction
plain_language_interpretation: When acute MI and broader ischaemic/coronary Heart disease occur together in the relevant sequence, WHO mortality rules support resolving the combination toward acute MI.
BNR_use: Promotes direct AMI above a lowest Part I line containing ischaemic/coronary heart disease from Possible to Likely when exclusions do not apply.
international_rule: M1 linkage: I20, I24 or I25 with mention of I21 acute myocardial infarction is coded to I21; WHO worked examples select myocardial infarction over ischaemic heart disease.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.2 Step M1 examples; 4.2.5 I20/I24/I25 with I21

topic: Hypertension with ischaemic heart disease / AMI
plain_language_interpretation: When ischaemic Heart disease/AMI is reported with hypertension in the relevant sequence, WHO mortality linkage rules support the Heart disease rather than hypertension as the selected cause.
BNR_use: Promotes direct AMI above a lowest Part I hypertension line from Possible to Likely when exclusions do not apply.
international_rule: M1 linkage: essential hypertension with mention of I20-I25 is coded to the ischaemic heart disease; acute MI is I21 within that range.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.5 I10 with I20-I25; analogous I11-I13 provisions

topic: Atherosclerosis with ischaemic heart disease / AMI
plain_language_interpretation: When ischaemic Heart disease/AMI is reported with atherosclerosis in the relevant sequence, WHO mortality linkage rules support the Heart disease rather than atherosclerosis as the selected cause.
BNR_use: Promotes direct AMI above a lowest Part I atherosclerosis line from Possible to Likely when exclusions do not apply.
international_rule: M1 linkage: atherosclerosis with mention of I20-I25 is coded to I20-I25; WHO examples similarly modify atherosclerosis toward IHD/MI.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.2 Step M1 examples; 4.2.5 I70 with I20-I25

plain_language_interpretation: When cerebrovascular disease is reported with hypertension in the relevant sequence, WHO mortality linkage rules support the cerebrovascular disease rather than hypertension as the selected cause.
BNR_use: Promotes direct stroke above a lowest Part I hypertension line from Possible to Likely when exclusions do not apply.
international_rule: M1 linkage: essential hypertension with mention of I60-I69 is coded to the cerebrovascular disease.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: When cerebrovascular disease is reported with atherosclerosis in the relevant sequence, WHO mortality linkage rules support the cerebrovascular disease rather than atherosclerosis as the selected cause.
BNR_use: Promotes direct stroke above a lowest Part I atherosclerosis line from Possible to Likely when exclusions do not apply.
international_rule: M1 linkage: atherosclerosis with mention of I60-I69 is coded to I60-I69; WHO examples similarly modify atherosclerosis toward cerebrovascular accident.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.2 Step M1 examples; 4.2.5 I70 with I60-I69

plain_language_interpretation: For mortality coding, coronary thrombosis is treated as myocardial infarction evidence unless the coding rules specify otherwise. BNR therefore treats this wording as direct AMI evidence.
BNR_use: Treats coronary thrombosis wording as direct AMI evidence for mortality classification rather than context-only wording.
international_rule: I24.0 coronary thrombosis not resulting in myocardial infarction is not used for underlying-cause mortality coding; for mortality myocardial infarction is assumed and assignment made to I21.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual

plain_language_interpretation: Clearly non-traumatic intraventricular or intraparenchymal cerebral haemorrhage belongs within the intracerebral-haemorrhage Stroke family. Explicit traumatic wording blocks this rule.
BNR_use: Adds non-traumatic intraventricular and intraparenchymal cerebral haemorrhage wording to direct stroke evidence; explicit traumatic wording blocks the direct rule.
international_rule: ICD-10 I61 is intracerebral haemorrhage; I61.5 is intracerebral haemorrhage, intraventricular. BNR uses this only for clearly non-traumatic wording.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 2016 classification and Volume 2 mortality instructions

plain_language_interpretation: BNR-Heart fatal-event surveillance is broader than certificates that literally say AMI. It includes compatible ischaemic/coronary Heart evidence. Sudden cardiac death is kept as uncertain evidence unless stronger Heart wording is present.
BNR_use: Defines the mortality surveillance family as explicit AMI plus compatible ischaemic/coronary heart disease evidence; sudden cardiac death alone is retained only as uncertain evidence, with certificate position/source structure determining Possible versus Mention.
international_rule: This is a BNR surveillance-scope decision, not an international ICD selection rule. Historical BNR sources distinguish clinical acute-MI event definitions from death-register ascertainment using IHD and sudden cardiac death.
source: Barbados National Registry CVD Annual Report 2023; Rose et al., Rev Panam Salud Publica 2016
section: Annual report Methods/Appendix C; Rose et al. methods and Figure 2a

plain_language_interpretation: BNR-Stroke mortality follows the established acute Stroke surveillance family: vascular Stroke/infarction or intracerebral/subarachnoid haemorrhage, while excluding TIA, traumatic and subdural/epidural causes.
BNR_use: Retains the BNR stroke definition for fatal-event classification: vascular neurological impairment lasting more than 24 hours or leading to death; excludes TIA, subdural/epidural haemorrhage, poisoning and trauma.
international_rule: This is the BNR surveillance definition derived from the WHO stroke definition; it guides which certificate expressions belong in the BNR-Stroke family but does not replace ICD mortality selection rules.
source: Barbados National Registry CVD Annual Report 2023; Rose et al., Rev Panam Salud Publica 2016
section: Appendix C BNR-Stroke; Rose et al. methods and Figure 2a

topic: Specified non-traumatic cerebral haemorrhage / bleed terminology
plain_language_interpretation: Anatomically specified, non-traumatic bleeding within the brain is treated as direct Stroke evidence because it maps to the intracerebral-haemorrhage family.
BNR_use: Treats anatomically specified non-traumatic cerebral, cerebellar, pontine, brainstem, thalamic, intraventricular or intraparenchymal haemorrhage/bleed wording as direct BNR-Stroke evidence.
international_rule: ICD-10 I61 covers intracerebral haemorrhage and the BNR acute-Stroke definition includes intracerebral haemorrhage; explicit traumatic wording remains excluded.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 classification; BNR Stroke case definition

topic: Generic non-traumatic intracranial haemorrhage as uncertain Stroke evidence
plain_language_interpretation: An unspecified non-traumatic intracranial bleed is compatible with Stroke but not specific enough to rule out every excluded haemorrhage type. BNR therefore keeps it Possible rather than Primary.
BNR_use: Places generic non-traumatic intracranial haemorrhage/bleed in Possible rather than Mention when no traumatic, subdural, epidural or extradural wording is present.
international_rule: ICD-10 separates intracerebral haemorrhage (I61) from other nontraumatic intracranial haemorrhage (I62). Because the BNR acute-Stroke definition excludes subdural/epidural haemorrhage, unspecified intracranial wording is retained as uncertain rather than treated as definite acute Stroke.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 classification; BNR Stroke case definition

plain_language_interpretation: Stroke can cause paralysis-related pneumonia and aspiration. BNR uses this relationship only for very simple certificate patterns so that the rule stays understandable and does not become a general causal engine.
BNR_use: Supports a narrow classification refinement when current Stroke evidence and aspiration pneumonia/pneumonitis form the only simple competing certificate relationship: Stroke immediately above a final aspiration line may be Likely; current Stroke in Part II with sole Part I aspiration remains Possible.
international_rule: WHO Step SP6 guidance treats diseases causing paralysis, including cerebral haemorrhage and thrombosis, as obvious causes of pneumonia; the same conditions are obvious causes of aspiration and inhalation. Pass 6 uses this only in the restricted certificate patterns stated in BNR_use.
source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 Volume 2 Instruction Manual
section: 4.2.1 Step SP6; 4.2.4 K Pneumonia; S Aspiration and inhalation
